newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London pick up on yen's slide.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London pick up on yen's slide.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London firmed on Friday, led by blue chip stocks which stood to gain from the yen's continued slide against the dollar, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index in London was at 1,361.78 by 1535 GMT, up 4.57 points or 0.34 percent from its previous London close and retracing some of the loss in Tokyo overnight. The 225-share Nikkei average ended down 171.39 points, or 0.95 percent, at 17,867.04.
"It's flight to quality and a flight to anything that's going to gain from dollar appreciation," one market-maker said.
"Nobody's chasing it (the index) up too much but they're quite happy to own stock in this market."
The yen slid through the 124.56 level against the dollar to set a four year low.

Sony was the most aggressively bought stock, traders said, and rose 37.5 yen from the Tokyo close to 8,497.5 yen. Other blue chips to gain were Honda Motors, up 50 yen to 3,290 yen, and Toyota, up 15 yen to 3,175 yen.

Construction sector companies and banks halted their overnight slide -- prompted by worries about the financial stability of Tobishima Corp -- and were stable in London compared with their Tokyo close, traders said.
"It's literally been a case of looking to the same usual names," one trader said. "Anybody that's exposed to the dollar has seen buying interest."
